stimulus.text: This photograph, taken from the air on August 9, 1945, shows the mushroom-shaped cloud rising over Nagasaki, Japan, after the second atomic bomb used in war was dropped that morning. A wide white cloud cap spreads at the top, a dark column of smoke rises beneath it, and smaller clouds drift below.
stimulus.source_note: Photograph of the Nagasaki atomic bombing, August 9, 1945, taken by Lieutenant Charles Levy from a B-29 (U.S. government photograph, public domain). Viewed before use; listed in the shared image pool as saq-set-26-q3. The catalog license note reads 'PD: pre-1930 / CC0,' which is wrong for a 1945 photograph; the correct basis is that it is a U.S. government work.

source: original; stimulus drawn from book-grounded figures and paraphrases (see source_note)
stem: Why did American planners consider invading Japan's home islands so costly that a new weapon seemed worth using?

options.text: Iwo Jima and Okinawa showed Japan would defend its home islands fiercely
Japan had already sunk every American ship in the whole Pacific Ocean
options.misconception: American ships were still fighting in 1945; Japan had not sunk the fleet.

options.text: American troops refused to fight in the Pacific at all anymore
options.misconception: American troops fought across the Pacific, including at Iwo Jima and Okinawa.

options.text: The Soviet Union had promised to defend Japan against invasion
options.misconception: The Soviet Union declared war on Japan in August 1945; it never promised to defend Japan.

rationales.A: Iwo Jima and Okinawa showed Japan would defend its home islands fiercely.
rationales.B: American ships were still fighting in 1945; Japan had not sunk the fleet.
rationales.C: American troops fought at Iwo Jima and Okinawa in 1945.
rationales.D: The Soviet Union declared war on Japan in August 1945.
rationales.general:
1. Background from the books: Iwo Jima cost about 7,000 American lives and Okinawa about 12,000.
2. Both were small islands, far from Japan itself.
3. Planners read those losses as a warning: an invasion of the home islands would cost far more.
4. That fear is the core of the case Truman's supporters still make for using the bombs.
Remember: planners judge the next battle by the last one, so compare the costs.

figures.caption: The mushroom cloud over Nagasaki, August 9, 1945
figures.alt: Aerial photograph of a huge white mushroom-shaped cloud rising above smaller clouds, with a dark column of smoke beneath it
